propositions: _build_jira_backend constructs an AcliClient transport without validating that JIRA_URL, JIRA_USER, and JIRA_API_TOKEN are present, allowing a wholly-unconfigured Cloud environment to build a backend that silently fails only at first API call.

Cloud adapter lacks the construction-time credential guard that DC has; DC fails loudly at backend creation when JIRA_PAT is missing, while Cloud builds a doomed backend with empty Basic-auth credentials that later surface as misleading 401/project-not-found errors.
Cloud requires Atlassian account email as JIRA_USER for Basic auth; a bare handle or accountId silently fails with 401 but should be rejected at construction with clear validation messaging.
The test test_cloud_build_backend_with_missing_credentials_does_not_fail_loudly pins the old silent-build behavior and must be flipped to assert loud BackendEnvError to achieve parity with DC.

test_the_cloud_factory_also_asserts_conformance uses invalid JIRA_USER (non-email) in its fixture; this must be updated to a valid email so the credential guard passes and the conformance assertion is still reachable.
